summary_rationale: Xpro India is a survivor with clean accounts, a genuine specialty capacitor-film franchise and an A-/A1 rated balance sheet that is close to net-cash-neutral, but its economics today are those of an unfinished capital project rather than a proven compounder. Consolidated revenue was flat between FY2023 and FY2026 (₹511 Cr to ₹505 Cr) while EBITDA before foreign-exchange effects fell from ₹74 Cr to ₹47 Cr, return on capital employed fell from about 25% to about 4%, and cumulative free cash flow over FY2025 and FY2026 was about -₹395 Cr as roughly ₹700 Cr was committed to two new dielectric-film lines. The plain-plastic Coex businesses (about 73% of revenue, 5-7% EBITDA margin on management's own range, one unnamed customer at 29.6% of revenue) have no moat, and the implied dielectric margin of about 16-23% sits far below the 35-55% management quotes. The capacitor-film moat is real in thin gauges and customer-specific qualification but narrow in standard grades, where Indian capacity (about 22,500 t including Jindal and SRF) already exceeds Indian demand (about 15,000 t) and no import duty protects the market. Management has delivered its financial and mechanical promises (early debt repayment, funding, line construction) but missed every commissioning date it set, by about 15 months at Barjora and 18-21 months in the UAE, and refuses segment margin disclosure. The business qualifies only conditionally: it needs the new lines to reach 70-80% utilisation, thinner-gauge mix and pass-through of resin costs before returns on capital can exceed the cost of capital. Operating indicators are mixed to improving (H1 FY2027 revenue +32.6%, new line EBITDA-positive in October 2026) but unproven on margin and cash conversion.
